units.title: A real perturbation law with finite canonical KL
units.classification: shared measure-theoretic construction for Exercise 1.7; not the complete exercise
units.statement: Let mu be a probability measure on any measurable space. Suppose f is real-valued, a.e. strongly measurable, uniformly a.e. bounded by a finite real M, and has mean zero. For all sufficiently small real epsilon, the affine density is at least one half almost everywhere, its literal nonnegative-density construction is a probability law, and its canonical extended-real KL equals the real compensated entropy integral embedded in the nonnegative extended reals. In particular the divergence is genuinely finite, not merely assigned a totalized real value.
assumptions: mu is a probability law on an arbitrary measurable carrier. No smooth Gibbs density or Euclidean geometry is required.

f is a.e. strongly measurable, |f| <= M almost everywhere, and its actual integral is zero. Its integrability is derived from the essential bound and finite measure. No pointwise representative, smoothness or compact support is assumed.

The neighborhood is an ordinary two-sided real neighborhood of zero and includes epsilon=0. No division by M or epsilon is used. Positivity, mass one, the RN representative and finite KL are conclusions, not supplied certificates.

steps.title: Choose a neighborhood that also handles the zero bound
steps.text: At epsilon=0 the product of the absolute values is zero, so continuity gives a neighborhood where it is less than one half. Combine this with the a.e. bound on f. The resulting closed interval contains every relevant density value; in particular the clipping in ofReal has no effect almost everywhere.
steps.lean: isOpen_lt and continuous_abs produce hsmall. The a.e. interval hinterval is obtained from abs_mul and abs_lt, not assumed.

steps.title: Prove the actual density has unit mass
steps.text: The finite probability measure and essential bound make f integrable, hence also the affine density. Now use linearity of the actual Bochner integral and the zero mean. Converting this nonnegative integral into a lintegral proves the literal withDensity measure is a probability measure.
steps.lean: Integrable.mono' derives hfi; integral_add and integral_const_mul give hmass. withDensity_apply and ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal construct hprob.

steps.title: Identify the Radon–Nikodym representative almost everywhere
steps.text: The law is absolutely continuous because it was constructed by withDensity. Its RN derivative equals the supplied nonnegative density almost everywhere. The previously proved nonnegativity then identifies the real-valued RN representative with the affine expression. This is an a.e. statement, not pointwise equality or a differentiability claim.
steps.lean: Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity₀ uses a.e. measurability; ENNReal.toReal_ofReal uses hpos. No canonical pointwise representative is invented.

steps.title: Produce entropy integrability on a fixed compact interval
steps.text: The compensated entropy function is continuous, including at zero. On the compact interval from the first step its norm has a finite bound. Since mu is finite, that constant is integrable. Composition preserves a.e. strong measurability, so domination proves the actual entropy integrand integrable.
steps.lean: IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn supplies a finite bound; continuous_klFun.comp_aestronglyMeasurable and Integrable.mono' derive hq. No entropy integrability binder is added.

steps.title: Identify finite KL itself, not only its real projection
steps.text: Transfer entropy integrability across the a.e. RN identity. The canonical equivalence gives integrability of the log likelihood ratio under the perturbed law. Apply Mathlib's formula for the extended-real divergence, then substitute the actual density. Its value is ofReal of a real integral, which cannot be infinity. A toReal identity alone would not establish this.
steps.lean: integrable_klFun_rnDeriv_iff and klDiv_eq_integral_klFun close the integrability branch; integral_congr_ae substitutes hrn. The focused test derives finiteness using ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top.

steps.title: Connect to the analytic parent without claiming the exercise
steps.text: This law identity is the measure-theoretic input to the already compiled compensated integral limit. A focused test actually composes the two results to obtain the real-valued canonical KL asymptotic, using nonnegativity before taking toReal. That example is not a separately published canonical theorem or Bench question. The source's Fisher limit, LSI admissibility and PI domain extension remain independent. Centering does not make a function compactly supported.
steps.lean: The owning module constructs the finite law/KL interface. Tests/Shared/BoundedPerturbationLaw.lean combines it with tendsto_integral_klFun_one_add_mul_div_sq using eventual equality and Tendsto.congr'; the example earns no extra public leaf.

units.lean_statement: The eventual conjunction records the density lower bound, actual probability-measure instance and exact ENNReal KL formula. The theorem uses no new project definition or hypothetical law witness.
units.lean_proof: A small-parameter interval gives integrability, mass one and an actual withDensity probability law; the canonical RN identity and compact entropy bound then select the finite branch of canonical KL. All intermediate facts are constructed inside one public theorem.
